# `enum-added`

Enum added to a free value

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `enum-added` (both directions), `enum-added-in-request`, `enum-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A free value became a closed set (an `enum` was added).

## Why this default

In requests: clients sending other values are rejected. In responses: clients receive a subset of values.

## Example

From test case [`enum-added`](../../test/cases/enum-added/): A free request string became an enum.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+           enum:
+           - a
+           - b
```

Findings:

- `enum-added-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  enum-added: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, keep the value free and validate it softly.
